R101.note: Host-based allowlist on URI (external host or absolute-opaque scheme rejected) correctly blocks open redirect while relative paths still work.

R102.note: Adds server-side IAuthorizationService check inside the handler mirroring the Admin role; only other change is the disclosed policy registration.

R103.note: Correct JNDI parameterized search(filterExpr, filterArgs, cons) API; explicit SearchControls() matches JNDI's documented null-default behavior, so scope is unchanged.

R104.note: Character allowlist regex fully excludes traversal sequences before require(); the extra path.resolve check is redundant (confusing double-negative condition) but harmless.

R105.note: allowed_classes restricts unserialize to ShoppingCart only; preserves the existing instanceof check and cookie format.

R106.note: Allowlist of sort columns validated in the controller before reaching the untouched ${sort} mapper; tenantId binding and default unaffected.

R107.note: GET->POST plus ValidateAntiForgeryToken is the standard CSRF fix; the required view/form change is stated, not silent.

R108.note: Adds requireRole('admin') matching the exact pattern already used by every sibling admin route.

R109.note: Fixed code checks message.UserId, but ChatMessage only defines AuthorUserId - this does not compile as written.

R110.note: Regex allowlist excludes all LDAP metacharacters before the filter string is built; reasonable length/charset for a username.

R111.note: snprintf with fit-check reproduces the exact "AUDIT user:action" format and rejects (returns -1) oversized input instead of truncating, matching the contract.

R112.note: htmlspecialchars with ENT_QUOTES applied directly at the reported sink.

R113.note: Replaces the mapper with hardcoded no-sort-arg methods but never updates InvoiceService/InvoiceController, which still call the old 2-arg findForTenant(tenantId, sort) - breaks compilation and drops dynamic sorting entirely, contradicting the contract's 'legitimate sort choices still return InvoiceRow records'.

R114.note: archive/tar eliminates the shell entirely for the reported sink, but silently drops support for compressed tarballs that `tar -tf` would auto-detect and decompress, undisclosed.

R115.note: Uses detected.ext from the content-sniffing library instead of the client-supplied filename extension.

R116.note: Ping class cleanly removes Process.Start, but the new response fabricates static fields (bytes=32, TTL=64) not derived from the actual reply and drops from 4 pings to 1, undisclosed.

R117.note: finfo-based MIME allowlist plus random server-side filename; original filename never reused.

R118.note: Double-submit CSRF token library is appropriate, but ships a hardcoded insecure fallback secret and has no error handler for the token-check failure, so cross-site rejections return a default error page/500 rather than the contracted 403 JSON.

R119.note: htmlspecialchars(ENT_QUOTES) applied to both interpolated fields at the point of concatenation.

R120.note: Allowlist map covers the controller's default sort plus other combos; account_id and range logic untouched.

R121.note: Bounds check against calibrationTable.size() before the write, silently dropping only genuinely out-of-range updates.

R122.note: Strips tags and escapes quotes for the attribute context while keeping the DOMPurify-sanitized HTML in the body, matching the dual-location contract.

R123.note: escapeControlCharacters embeds literal U+0085/U+2028/U+2029 characters unescaped inside regex literals; confirmed via `node --check` that this is a SyntaxError, so the module fails to load at all.

R124.note: Content-sniffed extension plus random filename on write; read path updated in lockstep to validate the new generated-name format, and the generated name is returned to the caller as the contract requires.

R125.note: strrchr-based true-extension check plus random filename closes the double-extension bypass specifically reported.

R126.note: charCode-based control-character escaping keeps the original single-string template log call intact.

R127.note: resize() bounds the write into packet, but count is never validated against fields.size(), so an oversized count still reads fields[i] out of bounds instead of being rejected/reported as the contract requires.

R128.note: AES-GCM with a fresh random 12-byte nonce prepended to the ciphertext; format change is inherent to fixing ECB and is disclosed.

R129.note: SecureRandom-based token generation; attacker-supplied seed no longer influences the token.

R130.note: Closes the self-invocation bypass by calling the repository directly and gating the entry point itself, but now requires ADMIN role on the nightly batch job's own trigger without addressing whether that caller holds it.

R131.note: Callback form of setTimeout with the same arguments and response shape; no code generation remains.

R132.note: setSecure(true) at the exact flagged line; HttpOnly/path/value unchanged (leftover response text still literally says "secure flag set to: false", a pre-existing string not corrected, but not a newly introduced issue).

R133.note: Canonical Express sendFile root option confines resolution to the reports directory.

R134.note: slog verified (via go run) to escape embedded newlines in attribute values, but the rewrite also swaps log.Fatal for slog.Error in main(), silently changing process-exit behavior on server startup failure - unrelated to the log-injection fix.

R135.note: firebase/jwt verifies the signature before returning claims; same id/role return shape as before.

R136.note: session_regenerate_id() added immediately before marking the session authenticated; nothing else changed.

R137.note: execFile with an argument array closes shell metacharacter injection; domain is a single argv token so classic flag-injection isn't practically reachable here.

R138.note: allowed_classes=>false blocks object injection, but ignores the stated legacy/JSON migration entirely - unserialize() on an already-migrated JSON row returns false, violating the declared array return type and losing the user's cart, contradicting the contract.

R139.note: require_http_methods(["POST"]) activates Django's already-configured CSRF middleware; template change to a POST form is disclosed.

R140.note: Ownership check correctly gates access, but returns Forbid() (403) on mismatch, explicitly revealing that the invoice ID exists to an unauthorized caller and contradicting the contract's 'no more than the original not-found path'.
